title: A cluster is just another boundary; sensed boundaries are clarified after, declared boundaries are held before looking inside (2026-11-07)

sections.name: narrative
sections.label: Narrative
sections.content:
A cluster is probably just another boundary.

Sometimes we sense them before we clarify them. But if we discover ab issue that keeps coming back, eg: how do we write and store decisions... There is obviously a boundary there. But we sense it first.

If I want to create a very clear boundary for automated development... An agent assisted editor.... Then I probably need to really take the time to hold it and understand it before I look at what's inside.

This is the human/AI peer collaboration

sections.name: source
sections.label: Source
sections.content: The owner, in conversation with Claude Code, 2026-11-07, answering the question whether the declared/sensed split of boundaries is right (the agent had proposed: the top boundary is declared, interior boundaries are sensed as cells grow dense; a boundary record carries parent, purpose, exclusions with reasons, axes, authority and revision condition); recorded verbatim.
